quick.summary: What to do after you lose an argument, and why it isn’t pretending.
quick.takeaway: Disagree before the decision. Commit after it.

beats.line: I argued against the plan and lost. Do I still work on it?
To ship the simple version first.
Then the next step has a name. Disagree and commit.
Isn’t that just pretending to agree?
No. You said your view. Now you help it succeed.
First, disagree openly, with reasons, before the decision.
Then, once it’s decided, commit fully. No quiet dragging.
If new facts appear, raise them. Old arguments stay settled.
I’d have built more. But I’ll make the simple version great.
That is it. You were heard, and the team moves.

quiz.question: Your team chose an approach you argued against. What does disagree and commit mean now?
options: Back the decision fully, and raise new facts if they appear
Do the work slowly to prove your point
Agree in the meeting, then complain later
quiz.explanation: You have had your say; now you help the decision succeed, and only reopen it with new facts.

quiz.question: Disagree and commit means hiding your view so the team looks united.
quiz.explanation: You state your view openly before the decision; committing comes after it is made.
